Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopSphere Inc. Q4 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone followed by your name and affiliation. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopSphere Inc.'s Q4 2023 earnings call. Joining me today are Jordan Hale, CEO; Taylor Brooks, CFO; Morgan Lee, COO; Casey Nguyen, CMO; Riley Patel, CTO; Jordan Kim, CDO; and Dana Torres, CSO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale, CEO of ShopSphere Inc.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q4 2023 performance, driven by accelerated GMV growth and expanding take rates, alongside disciplined pricing and promotional strategies. We saw significant growth in key metrics like active sellers and mobile engagement, with GMV up 25% year-over-year to $12.5 billion.

Our focus remains on enhancing seller performance and operational efficiencies. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our AI-powered personalization tools, which we believe will significantly boost conversion rates and customer lifetime value.

We are investing heavily in supply chain diversification and fulfillment network expansion.

We are focused on improving gross margins through product mix optimization and cost controls.

We are expanding our presence in high-growth regions like APAC and emerging markets.

We are enhancing our customer experience through advanced mobile app features and AR try-on capabilities.

Finally, we are committed to sustainability initiatives that reduce our environmental footprint while delivering cost savings.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Brooks, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jordan. Our Q4 2023 revenue was $4.8 billion, an increase of 28% year-over-year. Gross margin was 31.2%, driven by product mix shifts, moderated COGS inflation, fulfillment efficiencies, and lower returns through tech innovations. Let me unpack the gross margin story in detail. This 31.2% marks a 170 basis point improvement year-over-year and our sixth straight quarter of expansion, lifting full-year 2023 to 30.5%, up 240 basis points from 2022's 28.1%. We're outperforming peers like Amazon's North American retail at 23-25%, Shopify merchants at 28-30%, and Wayfair's 25-27% range, thanks to execution on product mix, supply chain, and fulfillment.

Product mix shift was the top contributor at about 100 basis points, as our private label portfolio scaled to 28% of GMV from 18% last year, yielding 45-50% blended margins versus 22-25% for third-party sellers. Standouts included ShopSphere Essentials home goods and private-label beauty, akin to Amazon Basics or Target's Good & Gather—Essentials kitchenware grew 35% YoY in GMV at 48% margins, offsetting fashion softness where we cut low-margin SKUs like Shein's fast-fashion plays.

COGS inflation eased, with raw materials for apparel and electronics down to +4% YoY from Q2's +12%, via multi-sourcing to Vietnam and Mexico for 8-10% lower landed costs post-tariffs. We hedged 70% of 2024 commodities, unlike Etsy's exposed craft suppliers.

Fulfillment added 80 basis points, with our 45 global centers—15 new in 2023—cutting costs to 12.1% of revenue from 13.8%. Per-unit shipping dropped 15% to $4.82 on 1.2 billion units, powered by AI dynamic routing across UPS, FedEx, and DHL. North America hit 98% same-day dispatch, trimming last-mile 22%; Europe's Warsaw hub saves 10% intra-EU.

Returns at 18.2% of units—high in apparel/beauty at 25-30%, matching Zalando/ASOS—improved 40 basis points via ML size recommendations and Virtual Fit AR on 80% of fashion, cutting apparel returns 14% quarter-over-quarter.

Regionally, North America led at 32.8% up 200 bps on scale and subscription perks; APAC at 29.1% despite yen weakness via Taobao electronics sourcing; EMEA at 27.4% hit by 5% promos against Shein/Temu, countered by flash sale exclusions.

Forward, MarginMax AI reprices 2 million SKUs daily for 3-5% uplift; drone pilots with Wing target 30% last-mile savings; owned reverse logistics cuts returns to $4 per unit; recycled packaging at 40% yields 2-3% COGS savings ahead of EU directives. We guide Q1 2024 to 31.5-32.0%, full-year 32.0-32.5%, assuming stable freight—no big Red Sea hits thanks to hedges.

Operating expenses were $1.2 billion, representing 25% of revenue. Our marketing spend rose 20% to $450 million, focused on high-ROI channels amid seasonality.

On seasonality, Q4's bimodal holiday pattern drove 51% annual GMV weighting, with Q3 ramp at 28% YoY to $3.2 billion setting up $6.8 billion Q4. Historicals: 48% Q4 in 2019, 52-55% pandemic peaks, 49% in 2022. Q3 beat by 300 bps on pull-forward buying, Pre-Cyber events at 15% GMV, AOV up 8% to $92 via bundling. Weather muted apparel 12%, rates hit durables flat. Supply chain held with 98% fulfillment, 8.2x turns.

North America +32% on OmniPrime Days, 28 million VIP members; Europe +18% tempered by pricing wars; APAC +45% on 618/Diwali quick-commerce. AI demand sensing at 92% accuracy, BOPIS at 25%, VIP boxes flatten Q1.

Take rate hit 19.2%, up 110 bps YoY to drive $1.45 billion marketplace revenue on $7.55 billion GMV. Pricing added 60 bps—commissions to 14.5%, FBN at 28% GMV with dynamic fees to $5.75; ads at 22%. Promos shaved 20 bps but SmartPromo capped depth to 25%, lifting repeats 15%. Mix: marketplace 68%, subscriptions 45 million at $139/year, home & garden 22%. North America 19.8%, Europe 17.9%, APAC 18.5%.

GMV totaled $12.5 billion, 25% YoY and 10% QoQ, beating 20-23% guidance by $800 million. Marketplace sellers up 28% to 2.1 million, NexAI lifted AOV 35% to $58, conversions 12%. North America 25% to $6.5 billion, APAC 32%, Europe 14%. QoQ beat on mobile at 72%, NexDash quick-commerce.

Seller metrics: 2.8 million actives, 28% YoY, 450k net new; retention 92%. Revenue per seller $48,200, up 16% on ads $12/month, FBN 65%, Seller Intelligence +22% conversions. Top 10% drive 55% GMV. APAC +40%, NA +12%.

Promos at 28% GMV drove 22% growth, 18% uplift, 35% traffic spike, conversions to 4.8%, 15 million orders. AOV $85 steady. Margin hit 180 bps from 25% depth, but 4.7x ROI via Dynamic Pricing. NA 25%, Europe 12%, APAC 40%. Shifting to subscriptions, 8 million members.

Net income for the quarter was $450 million, or $1.25 per share. We ended the quarter with $3.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are reaffirming our full-year guidance of $18-19 billion revenue, 32% gross margins, and 14-15% EBITDA.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan Lee to discuss operations.

Morgan Lee:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on fulfillment efficiencies and supply chain resilience. Shipping times improved by 20%. Fulfillment costs per order fell to $6.82, down 18% YoY from $8.31, full-year $7.42 vs. $8.75. Scale on 1.2 billion units spread fixed costs, saving $0.45. EchoFlow 2.0 WMS boosted picks 28% to 220/hour, 85% automation. Robotics 1,200 AGVs cut labor 22%, $0.32 savings; AI packing down weight 12%, $0.28; EchoDash 40% U.S. last-mile to $2.14, DoorDash/Uber ties 19% cut. NA $6.95 down 20%, Europe $7.45 down 12% via MFCs, APAC $5.92 down 22%. Returns $0.89 via AI prediction. $1.2 billion capex targets sub-$6.00 FCPO. We are implementing robotics and AI routing expansions.

Now I'll turn it over to Casey Nguyen.

Casey Nguyen:
Thanks, Morgan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from Prime Week events and personalized flash sales. Customer acquisition costs were steady at $22. Our brand awareness increased by 25%. We are focusing on social commerce and loyalty programs, with promos delivering 4.7x ROI while moderating intensity.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley Patel.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Casey. On the technology front, we've been focused on app redesigns and AR integrations. Our website uptime was 99.9%. Mobile app usage increased by 35% YoY, with 7.2 million downloads (32% YoY), DAU 2.4 million (35%), MAU 18.5 million (29%), 13% DAU/MAU. Conversions 5.8%, up 120 bps. iOS 62%, ASO/influencer campaigns; Day 1 retention 48%. React Native cut loads 40%, Firebase pushes +22% re-engagement, AR try-on +25% sessions. NA 6.4% conv, APAC 5.2%, Europe 4.9%. 15% capex to app exclusives like voice commerce. We're investing in GenAI personalization.

Now I'll turn it over to Jordan Kim.

Jordan Kim:
Thanks, Riley. Data science is a key focus for us. We've seen a 15% improvement in conversion rates because of AI demand sensing and personalization initiatives. We are also focusing on data privacy enhancements compliant with GDPR and CCPA.

Now I'll turn it over to Dana Torres.

Dana Torres:
Thanks, Jordan. Sustainability is very important to us. We reduced our carbon footprint by 25%. We are committed to recycled packaging across 40% of shipments and drone/electric fleet pilots for lower emissions.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will be conducting a question and answer session. [Operator instructions for Q&A session]. Our first question comes from Sarah Chen with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Can you elaborate on GMV growth versus guidance, especially QoQ acceleration and regional drivers?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, Sarah. Absolutely, our $12.5 billion GMV delivered 25% YoY and 10% QoQ, beating 20-23% guidance by $800 million. Marketplace sellers grew 28%, AI recs lifted AOV to $58, conversions up 12%. North America 25% on same-day scale, APAC 32% via live-streaming, Europe 14% with local warehouses. QoQ beat reflects mobile at 72% and quick-commerce upside—sets us up strong for holidays.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Patel with JPMorgan.

Mike Patel:
Great, thanks. On gross margins, what drove the outperformance and Q1 guide?

Taylor Brooks:
Hi Mike. The 31.2% expansion came from 100 bps mix shift to private labels at 45-50%, COGS moderation to +4%, 80 bps fulfillment to 12.1%, AR returns cuts. Peers lag, and next-gen like MarginMax AI and drones support 31.5-32% Q1, 32-32.5% full-year.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Wong with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Wong:
Thanks. For ops, details on fulfillment cost trends and efficiency gains?

Morgan Lee:
Thanks, Lisa. FCPO at $6.82 down 18% YoY on scale, automation—WMS picks +28%, AGVs $0.32 save, packing $0.28, owned last-mile $2.14. Regional: NA 20% drop, APAC 22%. Returns to $0.89 via AI. Capex drives to sub-$6.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays.

David Ruiz:
Solid results. Impact of promos on sales/profitability, and moderation plans?

Casey Nguyen:
David, promos at 28% GMV drove 22% growth, 18% uplift, 4.8% conversions, steady $85 AOV. 180 bps margin hit but 4.7x ROI via Dynamic Pricing. Regional variance: APAC 40%, shifting to subs 8 million strong. Q3 intensity to 25%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emma Larsen with Citi.

Emma Larsen:
Thanks. Mobile app metrics—downloads, users, conversions—and tech roadmap?

Riley Patel:
Hi Emma. 7.2M downloads +32%, DAU 2.4M +35%, MAU 18.5M +29%, conv 5.8% +120 bps. Retention 48% Day 1, AR +25% sessions. React Native, Firebase +22%. H2 DAU +30-35%, app-first merchants.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Singh with Deutsche Bank.

Raj Singh:
Appreciate it. Seller metrics—actives, revenue per—and retention drivers?

Jordan Kim:
Thanks Raj. Data backs 2.8M actives +28%, $48k rev/seller +16%. New 450k, retention 92%, ads/FBN/tools +22% conv. Top 10% 55% GMV. Seller University, APIs to 3.5M/55k 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sofia Grant with RBC Capital.

Sofia Grant:
Thanks team. On seasonality deviations and smoothing efforts?

Dana Torres:
Hi Sofia. Q3 +28% ramp beat on pull-forward, AOV +8%, but apparel weather hit. AI forecasting 92%, BOPIS 25%, subs flatten Q1. Q4 51% weighting resilient, targeting 45-47% long-term.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
